problem: A file worker committed but cancellation from fileChanged discarded its mutation metadata before ordinary tool completion. A second reproduced case lost a committed sandbox write after restart when the outer script never returned.
implementation: Host-created invocation UUID is persisted with its exact assistant batch before the worker starts; journal schema migration stores the UUID separately from the model tool-call ID.

A settlement notification precedes fileChanged, remains correlated after cancel/replacement, and never advances to the next tool. Direct committed output is retained; cancellation still stops remaining work.

Sandbox inner mutations bind to the original native outer request. Restart recovery creates an interrupted outer result when required, preserving actual file-change metadata without claiming that the script completed.
Fixed-agent journal lookup and exact invocation identity prevent a reused model call ID or forked chat from inheriting another turn mutation authority.
Failed dispatch persistence prevents filesystem mutation. Recovered history is persisted when a later UI queue committer is installed.

Direct/background sandbox calls without a current model invocation remain journaled without inventing an assistant turn; nonempty retired wire IDs are rejected before dispatch instead of being reclassified as idle background calls.

validation.platform: Windows 11, static Qt 6.11.2, GCC 16.2.0, offscreen QtTest
validation.scope: Actual AgentEngine + AgentToolHost + native QuickJS worker, controlled loopback model fixtures, temporary filesystem/journal fixtures only.

sharedFollowup.sourceBasis: Current sources after direct Engine generation and external RPC ownership rejection guards; before background sandbox owner classification correction.

repairGate.scope: Focused repair run after background owner classification and retired-wire guards. Not a full all-suite run.

startupHost.scope: Observed earlier shared run, not part of13-suite repair command; contains restart direct-unsettled and sandbox-settled-missing-result hydration cases.

limits: Process lifetime/restart fixtures establish these transitions, not universal power-loss guarantees. Pending prepared/recovery-required journal operations retain existing explicit recovery behavior.
Idle sandbox callbacks without an active outer model request remain visible through the chat journal; this does not invent an earlier model-turn owner.
Mutation dispatch binding requires the host durable history callback for restart attribution; standalone engines without persistence retain only in-memory history.
Current combined full-candidate integration remains pending; focused passing suites establish their tested scenarios only.
warnings: Runtime-app temporary-directory cleanup warnings remain visible in the retained passing report; they are not converted into an assertion of cleanup completeness.
sourceHashScope: Canonical LF observation of current integration sources. Concurrent fallback/picker integration is separate; retained reports, not these hashes alone, identify tested scope.
